summary: The Prophet ﷺ's first sermon in Madinah urged people to send good deeds ahead for the Aakhirah, and he gave a second sermon praising the Qur'aan and calling to the worship of Allah alone.
notes: Two separate sermons are reported in one narration (the first sermon, then 'another sermon').

summary: Sa'eed bin Abdur Rahmaan Jumhi reports the Prophet's sermon at the first Jumu'ah in Madinah, calling people to taqwa, the Aakhirah and the worship of Allah alone.
Hiraar reports the Prophet's address before a battle, reminding the Sahabah of the reward of the one who is martyred in the path of Allah.
Jaabir reports that at Hijr on the Tabook expedition the Prophet warned the Sahabah not to ask for miracles, recounting how the people of Saalih were destroyed, and named the one man who was saved.
Hasan bin Ali reports the Prophet's sermon on the Tabook expedition, telling people to seek a moderate livelihood and to look for sustenance through obedience to Allah.

Abdullaah bin Amr reports the Prophet's address after the conquest of Makkah, condemning unlawful killing, rejecting claims to a child that is not one's own, and giving rulings on adultery, prayer times and marrying an aunt and niece together.
Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address at the conquest of Makkah, setting the blood money for manslaughter and abolishing the killings and pride of the Period of Ignorance.
Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's address from his camel during the conquest of Makkah, teaching that taqwa, not lineage or pride, is what makes a person honoured before Allah.
Salmaan reports the Prophet's sermon on the last day of Sha'baan about the coming of Ramadhaan, its virtues, the reward for feeding a fasting person, and the four things to be done abundantly in it.
Anas reports that as Ramadhaan drew near, the Prophet ﷺ told people that on its first night every believer of the Qiblah is forgiven.

Ali reports the Prophet's first-night Ramadhaan sermon that the Shayaateen are restrained and du'aas are accepted, and then reports that the Prophet ﷺ devoted the last ten nights of Ramadhaan to worship and seclusion.
notes: Two reports are joined: the first-night sermon, and Ali's separate account of the last ten nights and what 'tightening the loincloth' meant.

summary: Jaabir reports the Prophet's sermon urging repentance, dhikr and sadaqah, stressing the obligation of Jumu'ah, and setting out who may and may not lead the prayer.
Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's warning that whoever lives one, two or three miles from Madinah and misses Jumu'ah will have his heart sealed.

Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address: Shaytaan has despaired of being worshipped in the land but still works through lesser sins, the Book and Sunnah are left behind, Muslims are brothers, and they must not kill one another.

Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon at Masjidul Khayf in Mina: whoever makes the Aakhirah his main concern will have his affairs set right and be made self-sufficient, while whoever makes this world his main concern will be scattered and poor.

Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's Mina sermon on three things a Muslim's heart never betrays, and Jaabir reports the Prophet's Farewell Hajj address on the sanctity of life and wealth, the abolition of Period of Ignorance debts and blood money, and the rights of women.
notes: Two reports are joined: Ibn Umar's Mina sermon and Jaabir's longer account of the Hajj sermon at Arafah and Bat Waadi.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports the Prophet's sermon on the day of Nahr, establishing the sanctity of the day, city and month, and charging those present to convey it to the absent and not to kill one another after him.
Jareer reports that at the Farewell Hajj, after asking for silence, the Prophet warned the people not to become disbelievers after him by killing one another.

Ummul Husayn reports seeing Usaamah and Bilaal with the Prophet ﷺ at the Farewell Hajj and hearing him tell the people to obey a leader who rules by the Book of Allaah; Abu Umaamah reports his further rulings on bequests, adultery, lending, debts, guarantees and a wife's spending.
notes: Two reports are joined: Ummul Husayn's account of the Farewell Hajj and Abu Umaamah's sermon from the same occasion.

summary: Abu Umaamah reports the Prophet's call from his camel to worship the Rabb, offer the five daily salaahs, fast Ramadhaan, obey the leader and so enter the Jannah of the Rabb.

Abdur Rahmaan Taymi reports the Prophet teaching the rites of Hajj at Mina and placing the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar in separate camps, and Raafi bin Amr Muzani reports seeing him preach on a mule while Ali repeated his words.
notes: Two reports are joined: Abdur Rahmaan Taymi's account of the rites and Raafi bin Amr Muzani's account of the sermon at Mina.

summary: Abu Hurra Raqaashi reports the Prophet's sermon at Mina during the days of Tashreeq on the sanctity of life, wealth and honour, the abolition of Period of Ignorance debts and blood money, and the rights of spouses; further reports add a similar sermon, Humayd's report of Hasan's remark, and Ibn Umar's account of the Surah Nasr occasion.
notes: Several reports are joined: Abu Hurra Raqaashi's sermon, Humayd's report of Hasan's remark, and Ibn Umar's similar report of the same sermon. Hasan is the Basri scholar, as Humayd Taweel's teacher.

summary: Jaabir bin Abdullaah reports the Prophet's farewell sermon in the days of Tashreeq, saying no Arab is superior to a non-Arab, nor a white person to a black person, except by taqwa.
Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's address at Arafaat on the sanctity of the day, month and city, his going ahead to the pond, and his warning about innovations introduced after him.

Abdullaah bin Umar reports that during the Farewell Hajj the Prophet ﷺ spoke at length about Maseeh Dajjaal, noting that every Prophet including Nooh warned his people of him, and that the Rabb is not one-eyed.
Safeenah reports the Prophet's description of Maseeh Dajjaal: his missing left eye, the word Kaafir between his eyes, his deceptive Jannah and Jahannam, and his destruction at Afeeq in Shaam.

Junaadah bin Abu Umayyah Azdi reports a Companion's narration of the Prophet's warning about Maseeh Dajjaal, describing his signs, his power to bring rain and his inability to enter the four Masaajid.
Abu Umaamah Baahili reports the Prophet's long sermon on Maseeh Dajjaal: his trials, his forty days on earth, and how believers should estimate the prayer times in those short days.
Jaabir reports the Prophet's sermon on the spy sent to investigate Maseeh Dajjaal and his statement that Maseeh Dajjaal cannot enter Madinah or Makkah, which are guarded by angels.
notes: The spy episode is only summarised in the text.

summary: Tha'laba bin Abbaad reports Samurah bin Jundub's account of the eclipse sermon, in which the Prophet ﷺ said eclipses are signs for people to repent, and warned that Qiyaamah comes after thirty liars and the one-eyed Maseeh Dajjaal.
notes: The OCR damage drops the opening of the Ya'jooj and Ma'jooj passage, so the sentence starts mid-way.

summary: Baqeera, wife of Qa'qaa, reports the Prophet's warning that when the earth is heard to sink in the west, Qiyaamah has arrived.
Baraa reports the Prophet's loud lecture condemning backbiting and the searching out of Muslims' faults, warning that Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for them.
Another narration adds the Prophet's words that one should not harm the Mu'mineen or search out their faults, because Allah exposes the faults of one who searches for his brother's faults.
notes: Unattributed addition from another narration, continuing the lecture in the previous report.

summary: Aa'isha reports the Prophet's sermon on enjoining good and forbidding evil, warning that prayers and requests will go unanswered if this duty is neglected.

Abdullaah bin Umar reports the Prophet's warning against oppression, lewdness and greed, followed by his answers on the best act of Islaam and the best Hijrah, and a further command about keeping trusts.
notes: Joins a second narration ('Yet another narration states') that adds a command about misappropriating trusts.

summary: Ayman bin Khuraym reports the Prophet's warning that false testimony is equated with shirk, Anas bin Maalik reports his warning against interest, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari reports his warning against the subtle shirk.
notes: Three separate reports are joined: Ayman bin Khuraym, Anas bin Maalik and Abu Moosa Ash'ari.

summary: Nu'maan bin Basheer reports the Prophet's saying that ingratitude for little leads to ingratitude for much and that unity is a mercy while disunity is a punishment; Abu Umaamah Baahili then advises sticking to the larger group.

Abu Dharr reports the Prophet's recitation of the Surah Saba verse about Dawood's thankfulness, and his teaching that fearing Allah in private and public, being just in anger and contentment, and spending moderately in poverty and wealth are gifts given to Dawood.

Ali reports the Prophet's lecture that the only good in life lies with the listener and the truthful scholar, and his praise of the Qur'aan in reply to Miqdaad bin Amr's question about the period of truce.

Husayn bin Ali reports the Prophet's lecture on abstinence from the world, reminding people of death and giving glad tidings to those who avoid searching for faults, earn purely, give Sadaqah from their excess and keep to the Sunnah.
